messages:
Lina Gomez: Heads up — morning invoice batch 2026-04-02 05:00 UTC mis-generated for a handful of customers. Some accounts missing GPU line items and a couple show a duplicate invoice for the same window. @Ethan can you take a look?
Ethan Wu: On it. Which customers and invoice IDs? Any emitter logs?
Lina Gomez: Affected customers: HoloRise, MeridianOps, and WattLabs. Invoice IDs I spotted: inv_820101 (HoloRise), inv_820107 (MeridianOps dup A), inv_820108 (MeridianOps dup B), inv_820113 (WattLabs).
Lina Gomez: Quick log excerpt from billing-emitter:
```
2026-04-02T04:56:45Z billing-emitter WARN invoice_retry: customer=meridianops retry_count=1 reason="batch-timeout"
2026-04-02T04:57:02Z billing-aggregator ERROR apply_filters: customer=holorise dropped_lines=1 reason="region-tax-map-mismatch"
2026-04-02T04:57:10Z billing-emitter INFO emit: invoice_id=inv_820107 lines=5 state=generated
2026-04-02T04:57:11Z billing-emitter INFO emit: invoice_id=inv_820108 lines=7 state=generated
```
Priya Singh: I think this is two separate bugs: 1) duplicate invoices due to emitter retry not deduping when prior job completes during backoff, and 2) missing GPU line for HoloRise because `region_tax_key` didn't map, which caused the aggregator to drop the GPU line when tax resolution failed.
Ethan Wu: Reproducer: aggregator filters out any usage line if tax lookup returns null. That was changed in 2026-02 to enforce compliance, but should fall back to default tax code instead of dropping. I'll re-run tax_lookup for HoloRise.
Ethan Wu: SQL to look for dropped usage by tax-null: `SELECT customer, usage_id FROM usage_lines WHERE period='2026-03' AND tax_resolved=false;`
Lina Gomez: Ran it — HoloRise had one GPU usage line with tax_resolved=false, WattLabs had two small GPU samples that were filtered earlier, MeridianOps had no missing usage but two generated invoices (one from retry).
Sam Ortega: Finance policy: rebills under $75 can be auto-approved. MeridianOps duplicate needs manager approval to void one and keep the canonical invoice. Which one should we keep?
Priya Singh: Keep the later one inv_820108 (it has the complete set from the successful run). Void inv_820107. We'll need to re-emit HoloRise and WattLabs corrected invoices.
Lina Gomez: Plan: 1) update aggregator to fallback to `tax_code:standard` when lookup failed, 2) re-aggregate HoloRise and WattLabs with `--include-tax-fallback`, 3) mark inv_820107 void (pending approval), 4) emit corrected invoices and notify customers.
BillingBot: automated: rebill-request queued — customers [holorise, wattlabs], requested_by=Lina Gomez, eta=15m.
Ethan Wu: I've pushed a hotfix branch to ensure emitter dedups on idempotency token: `fix/invoice-dedupe-retry-2026-04` and a patch to aggregator tax fallback. Running re-aggregation now.
Lina Gomez: Re-aggregation result (dry-run): HoloRise +1 GPU line (now tax_code=standard), WattLabs +2 small GPU lines restored, MeridianOps merging inv_820107+inv_820108 -> will keep inv_820108. Estimated delta across three: +$42 (net charge).
Sam Ortega: Manager approved voiding inv_820107 and reissuance. Finance signs off on rebills since < $75.
Ethan Wu: Performed void: inv_820107 status=voided; emitted inv_820119 (HoloRise corrected) and inv_820120 (WattLabs corrected). Emitted invoice for MeridianOps remains inv_820108.
BillingBot: automated: inv_820107 status=voided by=Ethan Wu; inv_820119 status=sent by=Ethan Wu; inv_820120 status=sent by=Ethan Wu.
Lina Gomez: Notifying support to send short explanation to customers and attach corrected PDFs.
Priya Singh: Filing postmortem ticket — add CI guard to prevent aggregator from dropping lines when tax lookup fails, and add emitter dedupe test. Also schedule a runbook update so support has templated messaging for small rebills.
Sam Ortega: Thanks team. I'll close the loop with MeridianOps' AM so they don't get confused by the voided invoice. :white_check_mark:
Lina Gomez: Thanks all — good catch. We'll follow up after the postmortem.
